program.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Transform the black DVD into a white DVD.
requirements.source_phrase: transform the black DVD into a white DVD

outcomes.description: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
outcomes.target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
outcomes.reference: The black DVD in the input image.

nodes.question: Is the DVD visibly white in the edited image rather than black in the source image?
nodes.criteria: Compare the same DVD in SOURCE and EDITED: pass if its visible body/surface has changed from black in SOURCE to predominantly white in EDITED; fail if it remains black or has not visibly changed to white; unknown only if the DVD or its color cannot be judged.
nodes.binding: The requested transformation requires the DVD to end visibly white, not black.
nodes.source_quote: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
nodes.endpoint: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
nodes.necessity: The quoted instruction explicitly requests changing the black DVD into a white one. Without the visible color change, the requested result is incomplete.

Retaining DVD identity is stated in the outcome description, but the instruction itself requests a color transformation and does not make identity retention a separate visual change to assess. Splitting the color change into multiple checks would duplicate the same endpoint.

nodes.question: Does the object corresponding to the small rectangular item near the center of SOURCE visibly change from black to white in EDITED?

Pass only if the corresponding object is identifiable and its visible surface changes from black in SOURCE to predominantly white in EDITED. Unknown if the source item cannot be reliably matched or its color/change cannot be judged.

The source image visibly has a small rectangular item near the center, while the edited image has white discs; requiring evidence that the edited white object corresponds to the source item prevents an unrelated or newly appearing disc from satisfying the requested change.

d1: The node’s visual judgment appears consistent with the images: the small rectangular item near the center in SOURCE is not clearly identifiable as a DVD, while EDITED shows two white discs, including one near the dark object. The trace may have bound the edited disc to the requested DVD without establishing that it is the same object, and its claim that the source DVD is the round disc near center-right conflicts with the visible source, where that area contains a dark irregular object. This is a binding/identity and evidence problem, not a transport or dependency failure. Refine the node to establish correspondence using the source object’s location, shape, and context before comparing color; distinguish a newly appearing white disc from a demonstrated transformation of the requested object. Preserve the rubric’s partial-progress distinction: if the requested object’s change is uncertain, do not turn that uncertainty into a confident pass or infer no progress solely from the aggregate reference label. The reference label constrains the overall result but does not establish which object is the DVD.
